shape: one realistic feature slice that walks the whole stack, so four documented rules are exercised by a single agent instead of four
what_it_tests: root AGENTS.md: @devdigest/shared has TWO physical copies and a contract change must land in both
root AGENTS.md: db/migrations/** is generated - change schema.ts and run db:generate, never hand-edit a migration
root AGENTS.md + server/AGENTS.md: any test importing test/helpers/pg.ts MUST be named *.it.test.ts
client/AGENTS.md: data access only through src/lib/hooks/* - no raw fetch in a component, query keys live in the hook file
why_it_should_discriminate: Every rule fails silently. Editing only the canonical contract copy still typechecks on the server; a hand-edited migration still applies; a DB test named *.test.ts still passes locally and only breaks the Docker-free CI lane.
None of it is derivable from generic Node/React knowledge - it is repo convention recorded in prose.
prompt: Runs can be cancelled, but we do not record who did it. Add a `cancelled_by` field end to end: the user id that cancelled a run, nullable. Contract, database column, the repository read that exposes it, a test for that read, and surface it on the run row in the UI.
isolation: git worktree - the agent edits freely, we grade the diff
assertions: A3 the new field name appears in BOTH copies
A4 server/src/db/schema*.ts touched (the column starts there)
A5 no pre-existing file under server/src/db/migrations/ was modified by hand
A6 any added test that reaches Postgres is named *.it.test.ts
A7 client data access goes through src/lib/hooks/* - no fetch( added inside a component
graded_from: git diff --name-only plus content greps over the worktree - file paths are facts, not phrasing
kept_separate: pointer routing (does the agent read the doc that 'Read when...' names) needs a NARROW task; on a wide task the agent reads everything and the measurement is meaningless
environment_limits: The worktree has no node_modules, so tsc, vitest and drizzle-kit cannot run. Agents are told to write the code and state what they would run. A5 therefore checks only that no PRE-EXISTING migration file was modified.

sampling.policy: two runs as a screen, escalate only what is ambiguous

read_as.2/2: consistent - the rule is followed; treat as settled
read_as.0/2: consistent - the rule is broken; treat as settled
read_as.1/2: unstable - says nothing on its own, re-run THAT assertion to 5 before drawing a conclusion

sampling.why: Full n=5 on every assertion is the expensive way to learn that most of them are stable. Iteration 5 of the onion-architecture eval is the counter-example that justifies escalation: n=2 read 'redundant', n=5 showed the rule was load-bearing in 2 runs out of 5.
